questions.question: Choose the word closest in meaning to “exacerbate” as used in: “Repeated postponements will only exacerbate the rift within the coalition.”
questions.questionHtml:
Choose the word closest in meaning to “exacerbate” as used in:

“Repeated postponements will only exacerbate the rift within the coalition.”
questions.solution:
Explanation:

Exacerbate means to make a problem worse; aggravate matches this precisely.

Assuage means to lessen the severity, the opposite sense.

Temporize means to delay making a decision to gain time, not to worsen something.

Mollify means to soothe or pacify, which also opposes the sense of worsening.

questions.questionHtml: Identify the sentence that contains a misspelt word.

options.text: The regulator decided to supersede the older guideline after the review.
options.html: The regulator decided to supersede the older guideline after the review.

options.html: Routine maintenance will be scheduled during off-peak hours.

options.html: Basic data hygiene is indispensible for secure operations.

options.html: Access to the archives is a privilege granted by the committee.

questions.solution:
Explanation:

“Indispensible” is incorrect; the correct spelling is “indispensable” (from “dispensable” + prefix “in-”).

questions.question: Fill in the blank with the most appropriate idiom: “With the metro suspended after the cloudburst, we had no option but to go by ____ for the last two kilometres.”
questions.questionHtml:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate idiom:

“With the metro suspended after the cloudburst, we had no option but to go by ____ for the last two kilometres.”
questions.solution:
Explanation:

“Shanks’s mare” (also “Shanks’s pony”) means travelling on foot, which fits the context of covering distance without transport.

“Hobson’s choice” means no real choice; “the high horse” refers to arrogance; “the grapevine” means the rumour network—none fit the idea of walking.

questions.question: Choose the best one-word substitute for “A short stay at a place during a journey.”
questions.questionHtml: Choose the best one-word substitute for “A short stay at a place during a journey.”
questions.solution: “Sojourn” means a temporary stay. “Odyssey” is a long adventurous journey, “excursion” is a short trip for pleasure (not a stay), and “transit” is the act of passing through a place, not stopping to stay.

questions.question: Choose the correct verb to complete the sentence: “The European Union, along with several partner countries, ____ preparing a plan to leverage frozen assets for Ukraine.”
questions.questionHtml:
Choose the correct verb to complete the sentence:
“The European Union, along with several partner countries, ____ preparing a plan to leverage frozen assets for Ukraine.”
questions.solution: The head subject is the singular noun “European Union.” The phrase “along with several partner countries” is parenthetical and does not change the number of the subject, so a singular verb (“is”) is required.

questions.question: Convert the sentence into passive voice (choose the correct option). Why didn’t the regulators impose stricter capital requirements on those banks?
questions.questionHtml:
Convert the sentence into passive voice (choose the correct option).

Why didn’t the regulators impose stricter capital requirements on those banks?

options.text: Why weren’t stricter capital requirements imposed on those banks by the regulators?
options.html: Why weren’t stricter capital requirements imposed on those banks by the regulators?

options.text: Why hasn’t stricter capital requirements been imposed on those banks by the regulators?
options.html: Why hasn’t stricter capital requirements been imposed on those banks by the regulators?

options.text: Why wasn’t stricter capital requirements imposed on those banks by the regulators?
options.html: Why wasn’t stricter capital requirements imposed on those banks by the regulators?

options.text: Why weren’t stricter capital requirement imposed on those banks by the regulators?
options.html: Why weren’t stricter capital requirement imposed on those banks by the regulators?

questions.solution: The subject in passive becomes “stricter capital requirements” (plural), so use weren’t + past participle (imposed) in the simple past to match “didn’t impose.” Options B (wrong tense and number), C (number mismatch: wasn’t with plural subject), and D (singular “requirement”) are incorrect.

questions.question: In the sentence “Before the consecration, the artisan agreed to mitre the wooden frame while the archbishop adjusted his mitre,” what do the two instances of “mitre” mean, respectively?
questions.questionHtml: In the sentence “Before the consecration, the artisan agreed to mitre the wooden frame while the archbishop adjusted his mitre,” what do the two instances of “mitre” mean, respectively?

options.text: To decorate with gold thread; a sacred altar cloth
options.html: To decorate with gold thread; a sacred altar cloth

options.text: To measure lumber precisely; a unit of metric length
options.html: To measure lumber precisely; a unit of metric length

options.text: To bevel‑join two pieces of wood at an angle; a bishop’s ceremonial headdress
options.html: To bevel‑join two pieces of wood at an angle; a bishop’s ceremonial headdress

options.text: To carve an inscription; a church pulpit
options.html: To carve an inscription; a church pulpit

questions.solution: “Mitre” as a verb means to make a miter joint by cutting pieces (often at 45°) to join at a corner, while “mitre” as a noun is the tall, pointed ceremonial hat worn by bishops. The other options confuse “mitre” with measurement (“meter/metre”), textiles, or church furnishings.

questions.question: In the sentence “The regulator deemed the proposal inimical to financial stability,” choose the best antonym of “inimical.”
questions.questionHtml:
In the sentence “The regulator deemed the proposal inimical to financial stability,”

choose the best antonym of “inimical.”
questions.solution: “Inimical” means harmful, hostile, or unfriendly; its precise opposite in this context is “conducive,” meaning tending to promote or help. “Adverse,” “malign,” and “antagonistic” all align with hostility or harm, so they are near-synonyms, not antonyms.

questions.question: Identify the type of the underlined adverb in the sentence: The Commission supports the plan; however, it insists on stricter oversight.
questions.questionHtml:
Identify the type of the underlined adverb in the sentence:

The Commission supports the plan; however, it insists on stricter oversight.
questions.solution: “However” links two independent clauses and signals contrast, functioning as a conjunctive adverb. It does not describe how (manner), when (time), or to what extent (degree) the action occurs.

questions.question: Question: Identify the segment that contains the conditional error.
questions.questionHtml: Question: Identify the segment that contains the conditional error.

options.text: If the regulator wouldn’t have issued
a prompt corrective action notice last quarter,
options.html: a prompt corrective action notice last quarter,

options.text: several smaller lenders could have failed,

questions.solution: In counterfactual past (third conditional), the if‑clause must use past perfect, not “would have.” Replace “wouldn’t have issued” with “hadn’t issued.” Correct: “If the regulator hadn’t issued a prompt corrective action notice last quarter, several smaller lenders could have failed.” The result clause “could have failed” is appropriately in the perfect modal form for a past hypothetical.

questions.question: Identify which sentence uses the past form of “hang” correctly. A) The portrait was hanged above the fireplace during restoration. B) The convict was hanged at dawn after the final appeal was rejected.
questions.questionHtml:
Identify which sentence uses the past form of “hang” correctly.
A) The portrait was hanged above the fireplace during restoration.
B) The convict was hanged at dawn after the final appeal was rejected.
questions.solution:
Use “hanged” exclusively for death by hanging; use “hung” for all other senses. Sentence B is correct because it refers to execution. Sentence A is incorrect because an object (portrait) should be “hung,” not “hanged.”


Correction for A: “The portrait was hung above the fireplace during restoration.”

questions.question: Fill in the blank with the option that is the best synonym for “subside” in context. “After the emergency liquidity support, market panic began to ____.”
questions.questionHtml:
Fill in the blank with the option that is the best synonym for “subside” in context.
“After the emergency liquidity support, market panic began to ____.”
questions.solution: “Subside” means to diminish or lessen in intensity; “abate” matches this meaning. “Proliferate,” “exacerbate,” and “intensify” all indicate increase or worsening, which contradicts the sentence context of panic easing.

questions.question: Select the incorrectly spelt word.​
questions.questionHtml: Select the incorrectly spelt word.​
questions.solution: “Occassion” is incorrect; the correct spelling is “occasion,” while “accommodate,” “pronunciation,” and “supersede” are correctly spelt in standard English.​

questions.question: Choose the best one-word substitute for: “A message or statement written in memory of a person who has died, especially as an inscription on a tombstone.”
questions.questionHtml:
Choose the best one-word substitute for:

“A message or statement written in memory of a person who has died, especially as an inscription on a tombstone.”
questions.solution: “Epitaph” is the inscription on a tomb in memory of the deceased. “Obituary” is a death notice published in a newspaper, “eulogy” is a speech or tribute (often delivered at a funeral), and “elegy” is a mournful poem, not necessarily inscribed on a tomb.

questions.question: Convert the following into direct speech: The Chief Electoral Officer said that polling would begin at 7 a.m. the next day across Bihar.
questions.questionHtml:
Convert the following into direct speech:
The Chief Electoral Officer said that polling would begin at 7 a.m. the next day across Bihar.

options.text: The Chief Electoral Officer said, "Polling will begin at 7 a.m. tomorrow across Bihar."
options.html: The Chief Electoral Officer said, "Polling will begin at 7 a.m. tomorrow across Bihar."

options.text: The Chief Electoral Officer said, "Polling would begin at 7 a.m. the next day across Bihar."
options.html: The Chief Electoral Officer said, "Polling would begin at 7 a.m. the next day across Bihar."

options.text: The Chief Electoral Officer said, "Polling begins at 7 a.m. the next day across Bihar."
options.html: The Chief Electoral Officer said, "Polling begins at 7 a.m. the next day across Bihar."

options.text: The Chief Electoral Officer said, "Polling has begun at 7 a.m. tomorrow across Bihar."

questions.solution: When converting indirect to direct speech, restore backshifted elements: “would begin” → “will begin,” and “the next day” → “tomorrow.” The reporting verb “said” remains, and time/place references revert to the speaker’s original deictic form. Options B, C, and D keep backshifted tense or mismatched time expressions.

questions.question: To fund its seasonal inventory build-up, the firm plans to ____ a short-term working capital loan from its bank.
questions.questionHtml: To fund its seasonal inventory build-up, the firm plans to ____ a short-term working capital loan from its bank.
questions.solution: In banking, the natural collocation is “take out a loan,” meaning to obtain or secure it. “Take over” means assume control of something, “take up” means begin or occupy, and “take off” means depart or rapidly succeed—none fit the context of obtaining a loan.

questions.question: Choose the word that is closest in meaning to “intransigent”​
questions.questionHtml: Choose the word that is closest in meaning to “intransigent”​
questions.solution: “Intransigent” means unwilling or refusing to change one’s views or to agree about something; “unyielding” matches this sense of refusing to compromise, while “tractable,” “amenable,” and “acquiescent” all imply readiness to be guided, persuaded, or to comply, which is the opposite meaning.​

questions.question: In the sentence “Keep your pants on; the tour bus will depart in five minutes,” what does the idiom mean?​
questions.questionHtml: In the sentence “Keep your pants on; the tour bus will depart in five minutes,” what does the idiom mean?​

options.text: Be patient and calm; wait without rushing.​
options.html: Be patient and calm; wait without rushing.​

options.text: Put on more appropriate clothing before leaving.​
options.html: Put on more appropriate clothing before leaving.​

options.text: Leave immediately without waiting for others.​

questions.solution:
“Keep your pants on” is an informal imperative meaning “be patient” or “calm down,” commonly used when someone is impatient or in a hurry, so option A captures the idiomatic sense.​
Options B, C, and D reflect anger, literal clothing, or urgency to leave, none of which match the idiomatic usage documented in dictionaries and idiom references.​

questions.question: Read the passage carefully and answer the following questions: The European Union is navigating a difficult balance between long-term strategic ambition and short-term economic pressures. On one hand, the bloc is pushing policies to strengthen competitiveness across the single market, deepen capital access for innovative firms, and accelerate the green and digital transitions. On the other, it faces industrial cost headwinds, supply chain fragility, and uneven productivity across member states, which test unity and demand targeted reforms. Security has moved to the center of EU policymaking, with renewed emphasis on defence cooperation, resilience of critical infrastructure, and coordination with international partners. At the same time, the EU is refining migration and border management frameworks while attempting to uphold humanitarian standards and improve burden-sharing among members. Digital policy remains a flagship: the Union is advancing rules to promote fair competition, rein in systemic risks, and encourage responsible adoption of emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence. Climate policy also remains foundational, with discussions focusing on how to align ambitious emissions reductions with the need to keep European industry competitive and jobs secure. Enlargement adds another layer of complexity, as the EU evaluates governance, financing, and institutional capacity to integrate new members without diluting decision-making effectiveness. Throughout, the EU’s institutions are working to maintain trust—through transparency in rulemaking, stronger engagement with civil society, and clearer communication about the trade-offs inherent in major transitions. In this environment, pragmatic sequencing, regulatory coherence, and stable investment signals are likely to determine whether the Union can convert its policy agenda into durable, widely shared prosperity. According to the passage, what is identified as the EU’s central challenge going forward?

options.text: Execution: converting a broad policy agenda into tangible gains in productivity, security, and living standards
